prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"I need a really strong, heavy wine from Portugal that tastes like herbs to use when everyone drinks to the bride and groom."

List A:
Wine 1: Portuguese Red, Portugal, $14. Tasting note: "Portugal's popular brand is a lively, fresh, spice- and dried fruit-flavored wine. There are flavors of pound cake and nutmeg surrounding a core of solid, firm tannins. Great with food, this is not for aging."
Wine 2: Portuguese Red, Portugal, $10. Tasting note: "Spanish producer Vicente Gandia has made a foray into Portugal with this ripely fruity and soft wine. It is fresh, herbal and spicy with attractive red berry fruits. It's been made to be drunk young and it's ready now."
Wine 3: Rosé, France, $26. Tasting note: "From one of the old Provence estates, this is a concentrated herbal wine. It has plenty of spice as well as full red fruits and balanced acidity. This is a fine wine, packed with taste. Drink now."
Wine 4: Portuguese Red, Portugal, $10. Tasting note: "High-acid red wine is not for everyone, but this one—dry, stalky and light—is a genuine example of a wine that has always had a following in northern Portugal, great for pairing with fresh sardines. Think that way, and it's more than just a curiosity."
Wine 5: Sauvignon Blanc, France, $17. Tasting note: "This attractive herbal and spicy wine is the entry-level wine at this showcase estate. The wine is rich, generous with a character that reveals both crisp fruit and ripeness. That makes it rich and very drinkable young."

List B:
Wine 1: Portuguese White, Portugal, $23. Tasting note: "A rich, fruity wine from the north of Portugal. It has creamy apple and citrus flavors, a light and mineral texture and bright acidity. Drink now."
Wine 2: Portuguese Red, Portugal, $8. Tasting note: "A popular wine in Portugal, this is ripe, full of black fruits and with a lightly stalky aftertaste. It is rich and fruity, softly tannic with a full-bodied structure. It is easy to drink young."
Wine 3: Bordeaux-style White Blend, France, $15. Tasting note: "A crisp herbal wine, this is bright with acidity and citrus and gooseberries. It is lively, tangy and packed with fruitiness from its 50-50 blend of Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon. Drink this refreshing wine now."
Wine 4: Sauvignon Blanc, France, $25. Tasting note: "This attractive, herbal wine has intense fruitiness but misses any sense of place. It has appealing white currant and grapefruit flavors and a tight finish of acidity. Drink now."
Wine 5: Portuguese Red, Portugal, $48. Tasting note: "This wine has fine tannins, ripe berry fruits and well-integrated acidity. Rich and juicy, it offers blackberry flavors and a crisp aftertaste. Drink this wine, part of a range of wines from across Portugal, from 2018."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
